title: Histone Expression in the Aging RPE
text:
Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is the most common cause of irreversible vision loss in the world.
The scientific understanding of the aging retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and molecular mechanisms that
trigger AMD progression and RPE cell death are critical to discovering potential therapeutic targets for this
blinding disease. This proposal will determine signature of histone expression during RPE aging and the
impact on RPE gene expression, RPE cell death, and AMD progression.

title: Vascular-targeted Atheroprotective Gene therapies to Prevent Vein Graft Failure
text:
Over 30-50% of autologous vein grafts (VG) used to treat coronary artery disease and occlusive peripheral
arterial disease fail within 5-10 years of surgery due to intimal hyperplasia (IH). To address this unmet clinical
need, we propose to bioengineer VG with the potent atheroprotective molecule A20, using advanced AAV and
circular RNA gene therapy (GT) platforms. This first-in-class therapy that can be directly implemented on the
operating table will be tested in two relevant animal models of VG failure, in prelude for clinical translation.

title: Dopaminergic Regulation of Spatial Learning
text:
In this project, we will study the cellular and circuit mechanisms of spatial learning, and specifically its relationship to
dopamine release during body movements. This is particularly clinically relevant because dopamine signaling and spatial
learning are disrupted in multiple neurodegenerative disorders. Thus, this project has the potential to illuminate the origins
of spatial learning defects in neurodegenerative conditions, as well as the role of dopamine signaling abnormalities.

title: A Divergent Platform to Chemically Redesign Bioactive 5-8-5 Terpenoids
text:
PROJECT NARRITIVE
The proposed research is relevant to public health because it focuses on the chemistry and biology of terpenoids
with impactful pharmacological profiles. The objective of this proposal is to use these complex natural products
as a starting point to develop prototype chemotherapeutics for cancer. For this reason, the proposed research
is relevant to the NIH’s mission of developing fundamental knowledge that enhances human health.

title: Chemosensory Training Program (CTP)
text:
The Chemosensory Training Program at FSU affords pre-and post-doctoral trainees with unusually
broad and deep opportunities to explore and master many research approaches to important questions
about taste and smell function, whose loss involves devastating quality of life and whose central brain
circuits are important in obesity, eating disorders, hypertension and other neurological disorders.

title: Novel GluN2BR Radioligand for PET Neuroimaging in Alcohol Use Disorder
text:
This K99/R00 proposal will perform first-in-human characterization of the novel GluN2BR PET neuroimaging
radiotracer (S)-[18F]OF-NB1 (K99 phase), anticipating its application in people with AUD and healthy controls
(R00 phase). We will investigate the relationship between GluN2BR availability and alcohol-related behaviors,
particularly alcohol seeking and consumption, to uncover neurobiological drivers behind AUD. This
groundbreaking research promises to yield critical translational insights and foster the development of targeted
AUD therapeutic strategies.

title: Elucidating the role of ketone bodies in hepatic PUFA homeostasis and MASLD-MASH progression
text:
This research is highly relevant to public health as metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease
(MASLD) and steatohepatitis (MASH) are rapidly growing causes of liver disease globally, with scarce
treatment options currently available. By exploring the role of ketogenesis within remodeling of liver
polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) pools, and the impact this has on hepatic steatosis and liver injury, this study
seeks to uncover novel therapeutic pathways that could be leveraged to reduce liver injury, inflammation, and
fibrosis in MASLD-MASH patients. Understanding the role of ketone bodies within supporting hepatic PUFA
homeostasis, and the implications this has on the natural history of MASLD-MASH, may lend support for
interventions such as ketogenic or low-carbohydrate diets as potential strategies to address these widespread
metabolic diseases, and/or to develop pharmaceuticals targeting liver ketogenesis and PUFA biosynthesis to
resolve or slow MASLD-MASH progression.

title: High-throughput identification and characterization of conserved regulators of drug-induced plasticity using single-neuron resolution atlases of the complete Caenorhabditis elegans nervous system
text:
Chronic exposure to drugs such as psychostimulants produces long-lasting molecular
and functional changes in the brain, which in vulnerable individuals result in behavioral
changes that further predispose them to loss of control in their drug use and
progression of Substance Use Disorder (SUD). These drugs produce remarkably similar
behavioral outputs and act on similar molecular targets in the nervous system (brain
equivalent) of the simple yet powerful model organism Caenorhabditis elegans. In this
proposal, we leverage the capabilities for high-resolution, large-scale, and rapid genetic
analysis of the entire nervous system in C. elegans to identify candidate regulators of
long-lasting drug-induced changes and open up novel avenues of therapeutic
interventions for SUD.

title: Resources and workforce development for the New England Regional Biosafety Laboratory
text:
The New England Regional Biosafety Laboratory (NERBL) seeks to develop and maintain RBL containment
staffing that is proficient in core competencies to support building, laboratory and vivarium operations, with
embedded cross-training to ensure functional redundancies that sustain facility functions. Additionally, we will
expand capacities and expertise in key infectious diseases including Mycobacterium tuberculosis and influenza.
Achieving these milestones will ensure that the NERBL is sufficiently prepared to respond to pandemic and
emerging disease threats as they arise.

title: TCR signaling regulated T cell exhaustion in response to chronic viral infection
text:
Successful control of chronic viruses, such as HIV and HCV, greatly depends on vigorous and well-coordinated
CD4+ and CD8+ T cell responses. This study aims to identify cellular and molecular mechanisms, as well as
rational designs of therapeutics, that favor the formation and function of effector CD8+ T cells. The goal is to
help CD8+ T cells remain effective and avoid exhaustion, which is essential for treating chronic infections and
cancer.

title: Elite controllers as a model for a cure of HIV-1 infection
text: Elite controllers represent a model for a functional cure of HIV-1 infection, but underlying mechanisms enabling such a remarkable disease outcome are ill-defined. Here, we propose to use novel high-resolution single-cell technologies to analyze how immune responses in elite controllers can recognize, target and eliminate HIV-1 reservoir cells.

title: The Duke Center for Combinatorial Gene Regulation: multigenic control of gene expression in health and disease
text:
Many aspects of human health and disease involve dozens to hundreds of genes. In contrast, biomedical
research often focuses on individual genes. The goal of the Center for Combinatorial Gene Regulation is to
enable studies of the impacts of many genes at once in human health and disease.

title: Single molecule dissection of Arp2/3 complex activity and regulators in living cells
text:
Arp2/3 complex-based actin assembly is at the heart of cellular mechanics, motility and tissue homeostasis, and
is dysregulated in cancer and many other diseases (autism, depression, colitis and more). The integrated
mechanisms connecting the biochemistry and cell biology of Arp2/3-actin network driven processes are
undefined in most cases, making it difficult to chart effective therapeutic action. This program innovates a solution
to this gap in knowledge with an approach to precisely locate key biochemical activities in time and space within
living cells using the latest microscopic and genetic advances.

title: Role of breast cancer secreted miRNA in brain metastasis
text:
Breast cancer metastasis to the brain is rising in prevalence and is an increasingly lethal threat to the patients.
Our research objective is to determine the mechanism by which microRNA secreted by breast cancer cells
alters normal cells in the brain to promote metastasis. This understanding could help researchers develop
novel predictive biomarkers and therapeutic treatments to prevent cancer cells from metastasizing to the brain.

title: Mapping the Structural Basis for Mechanistic Diversity in Metalloenzyme Superfamilies
text:
Metalloenzymes perform challenging but essential transformations of inert chemical bonds in biological
systems. We seek a unified understanding of how different metalloenzyme superfamilies control metal ion
usage and reaction outcomes. These efforts will enable protein engineering or targeting of metalloenzymes for
inhibition in pathogens.

title: TYK2 Fusions in Lymphoma
text:
We propose to investigate the oncogenicity and signaling consequences of expression of a genetic abnormality
affecting a gene known as TYK2, a cancer driver gene discovered to be recurrently altered in human T-cell
lymphomas. Our studies will also investigate the possibility that oncogenic TYK2 and its downstream signaling
modules may be precision therapeutic targets in these cancers.

title: Alcohol Metabolism Disrupts Hepatic Thiol Redox Signaling and Control
text:
Alcohol toxicity is a leading cause of liver disease. The long-term goal of this research project is to investigate
how alcohol changes protein signaling and activity in the liver through modification of cysteine and lysine
amino acid residues. We will study these processes to better understand how alcohol-associated liver disease
occurs and to develop targeted therapeutic interventions to protect the liver from alcohol toxicity.

title: Development of Real-World Motor Outcome Measures in Ataxia-Telangiectasia
text:
Promising disease-modifying therapies are being developed for ataxia-telangiectasia and other pediatric
neurological diseases, but current assessment tools are very insensitive at determining efficacy, resulting in
large and expensive trials. This project aims to develop precise motor outcome measures, using inexpensive
and widely accessible digital technologies, that can sensitively determine if a therapy is effective in children of
all ages.

title: Metabolic DNA Damage as a Driver of Obesity-Linked Prostate Cancer Progression
text:
Prostate cancer is more aggressive and deadly in men with obesity and metabolic dysfunction, contributing to
striking disparities in survival outcomes. This project will determine how a toxic metabolic by-product called
methylglyoxal damages DNA and disrupts repair processes, promoting tumor growth and therapy resistance.
The results will identify new metabolic and DNA-repair targets that can guide precision prevention and treatment
of aggressive prostate cancer.

title: Cell cycle and checkpoint variations in development and disease
text:
How cells divide, grow, and respond to stress differs among tissues and is perturbed in disease,
but the molecular mechanisms for these variations remain incompletely understood. This
proposal seeks to fill this knowledge gap through investigation of a variant growth program
known as the endocycle and by defining new functions of the p53 tumor suppressor. The long-
term outcomes will ultimately have a major positive impact on human health by leading to the
development of new diagnoses and therapies for developmental malformations and cancer.
